vnmap

vnmap makes publication-ready choropleth maps of Viet Nam in R. It follows the compact API of usmap, while accounting for Viet Nam’s July 2025 administrative reform.

Installation

Install the current development version directly from GitHub with either remotes or pak:

# Using remotes
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ura8107/vnmap")

# Or, using pak
install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("ura8107/vnmap")

The repository must be public for anonymous installation. For a private repository, set a GitHub personal access token before installation, for example with Sys.setenv(GITHUB_PAT = "...").

Quick start 

library(vnmap)
library(ggplot2)

plot_vnmap()

example <- data.frame(
  province = province_info()$name_en,
  value = seq_len(34)
)

plot_vnmap(data = example, values = "value", id = "province",
           color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c()

Current commune boundaries use the same province identifiers and carry an explicit geography vintage:

hanoi_communes <- vn_map("communes", province = "Ha Noi")

Use the NSO-published reform workbook when joining pre-July-2025 commune data. A former unit may map to multiple current units where its territory was divided; relation == "part" records that fact, but no unpublished allocation weights are inferred. The workbook is downloaded explicitly because its redistribution terms have not been established; it is not bundled with vnmap.

path <- download_administrative_crosswalk(tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx"))
administrative_crosswalk(path, current = "00004")
administrative_crosswalk(path, province = "Ha Noi")

Transport facilities can be queried and layered in the same way:

infrastructure(type = "aerodrome", province = "Ha Noi")

plot_vnmap() + geom_infrastructure(type = c("port", "aerodrome"))

The snapshot contains 42 aerodrome entities, 80 named OSM industrial-port features, 32 border-control entities, and nationwide OSM trunk-network segments. Categories are deliberately conservative: aerodrome does not mean scheduled commercial service and port does not mean seaport. Use infrastructure_class, service_type, facility_roles, and status_source before constructing access or treatment variables. All data are community mapping rather than an official register. Network lines are generalized to 100 metres and are intended for statistical accessibility analysis and graphics, not routing or navigation. Railway yards, sidings, spurs and industrial lines are separately classified, and line features use province_codes for actual polygon intersections rather than a fabricated single-province owner.

The package also includes official 2024 population and regional-economic indicators. This produces a GRDP-per-capita choropleth for the current units:

data(province_stats_2024)

plot_vnmap(
  data = province_stats_2024,
  values = "grdp_per_capita_million_vnd",
  id = "code",
  color = "white",
  linewidth = 0.2
) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Million VND\nper person")

Documentation

The complete package reference manual is available as vnmap.pdf. After installation, the same function documentation is available from R:

help(package = "vnmap")
?plot_vnmap
?vn_map

Maintainers can regenerate all .Rd files and the PDF manual with:

Rscript tools/build-manual.R

Web app assets

A deterministic handoff for ura8107/vietnam-calendar exports the current 34-unit boundaries as WGS84 GeoJSON, the bundled 2024 statistics as CSV, and a lightweight SVG demo generated by plot_vnmap():

make calendar-assets
make verify-calendar-assets

See app-assets/vietnam-calendar/README.md for the exact file contract, JavaScript join key, copy command, coordinate system, and statistical caveats.

Administrative geographies

The current 34-unit geography is the default. The 63-unit geography used immediately before 1 July 2025 remains available for historical data.

vn_map()                              # 34 current units as an sf object
vn_map("provinces_63")               # historical 63-unit geography
plot_vnmap(include = c("Hà Nội", "Bac Ninh"))
province_code(c("Đà Nẵng", "Da Nang", "Danang"))
province_info("79")

Identifiers accept official two-digit administrative codes and names with or without Vietnamese diacritics. province_info() provides a clean join table.

Socio-economic regions

Every unit is tagged with one of the six General Statistics Office socio-economic regions. Select whole regions with region, or look the region up directly.

plot_vnmap(region = "MRD", labels = TRUE)   # Mekong River Delta
province_region(c("HCMC", "Can Tho"))
province_info()[c("name_en", "region_code", "region_en")]

Lower-level geographies

Optional historical district ("districts_63") and commune ("communes_63") layers cover the pre-July 2025 second and third administrative levels, which the reform abolished and merged. They are large, so they are not bundled; generate them locally with data-raw/build_adm2.R and data-raw/build_adm3.R, then filter to a province. Commune names are not unique nationwide, so always scope commune maps with province.

# after Rscript data-raw/build_adm3.R
vn_map("communes_63", province = "Ha Noi")

Working without sf

The name, code, and region lookups (province_code(), province_info(), province_region()) and the bundled statistics work without the sf package. Only the geometry functions (vn_map(), plot_vnmap(), vnmap_crs()) require sf.

Industrial parks

The bundled industrial-park snapshot can be filtered using current or former province names and added directly to an ordinary ggplot2 map:

industrial_parks(province = "Dong Nai", geometry = "point")

plot_vnmap(include = "Dong Nai", color = "white") +
  geom_industrial_parks(province = "Dong Nai")

Mapped site boundaries are returned as polygons; parks without a redistributable boundary use representative points. Every row carries source and location precision fields. The snapshot is intentionally conservative and does not replace the Vietnamese government’s legal register of established parks.

category separates designations that Vietnamese law does not treat as interchangeable. The default is the register scope, khu cong nghiep (industrial_park) plus khu che xuat (export_processing_zone); khu cong nghe cao (hi_tech_park) and the provincial-tier cum cong nghiep (industrial_cluster) are returned only on request.

industrial_parks(category = "industrial_cluster")
industrial_parks(category = NULL)   # every designation

A park mapped in several pieces - phases, an expansion, a site split by a road - is one record; part_count and osm_ids say how many OpenStreetMap features it came from.

Reading and writing basic information

industrial_parks_template() writes the columns a user may fill in, and industrial_parks() reads them back through attributes. A row whose id already exists updates that park; a row with a new id adds a park, which is how a park missing from the snapshot gets onto the map. Only non-empty values are applied, and every changed or added row is marked attribute_source = "user".

industrial_parks_template("parks.csv", province = "Dong Nai", blank = TRUE)
# fill in parks.csv, then:
parks <- industrial_parks(province = "Dong Nai", attributes = "parks.csv")
plot_vnmap(include = "Dong Nai") + geom_industrial_parks(data = parks)

write_industrial_parks() exports a layer as CSV, GeoJSON or GeoPackage. CSV output drops the geometry and adds longitude and latitude, so it can be edited and fed straight back through attributes.

write_industrial_parks(parks, "parks.geojson")

Coverage

The snapshot holds mapped locations for a fraction of the national register: data-raw/industrial-parks-audit.csv reports the mapped count against the 478 established parks in the Foreign Investment Agency’s November 2025 report. Parks with no redistributable mapped location are absent rather than placed at a province centroid; attributes is the supported way to add them.

Economic and policy zones

economic_zones() provides a deliberately conservative, evidence-graded snapshot of coastal and border-gate economic zones, export-processing zones, and named high-tech parks. Legal document numbers, dates, and direct official URLs are retained only where verified; missing row-level evidence remains explicit. Point accuracy is recorded for every row.

economic_zones(type = "national_high_tech_park")
plot_vnmap() + geom_economic_zones(type = "coastal_economic_zone")

The snapshot retains 20 coastal and 26 border-gate catalogue records matching current officially reported aggregate counts. Names without verified row-level instruments are labelled candidate_or_count_reconciled, not established. It also retains three named high-tech parks without claiming national completeness, and the three EPZs in the current Ho Chi Minh City official annex. The EPZ population is subnational and must not be described as a national register. Where no reusable zone geometry was verified, the record is retained at a deterministic pre-2025 province interior point with location_accuracy = "province_only" and geometry_available = FALSE. Industrial parks remain separate even when they lie inside an economic zone.

Data provenance

The historical 63-province geometry is derived from the public-domain geoBoundaries VNM ADM1 release. Current communes come from a pinned MIT-licensed community dataset derived upstream from Viet Nam’s Administrative Units Reference Map; current province polygons are dissolved from those exact commune polygons. Both are generalized for statistical plotting and are not legal-boundary products. The data-raw/ directory contains the complete reproducible build.

province_stats_2024_63 contains official 2024 area, average population, population density, and preliminary GRDP per capita from Viet Nam’s General Statistics Office PX-Web. province_stats_2024 aggregates those values to the current 34 units: population and area are summed, density is recalculated, and GRDP per capita is population-weighted. The source values are rounded, so aggregated results are estimates. Run Rscript data-raw/fetch_nso_stats.R to refresh the statistical datasets from the official tables.

The historical source vintage is 2008; the current source is an observed 25 July 2026 snapshot. Always select the geography matching the data period.
